design.imageDirection: Use abstract and illustrative concept imagery throughout, never company-project photography, portfolio mockups, actual staff depictions or client logos. Anchor the artwork in ink and off-white, with restrained deep plum, teal and coral accents. Keep text outside the images and compositions spacious. Image 0: a panoramic field of oversized geometric forms with a crisp negative-space opening. Image 1: a quiet paper-like composition balancing a dark plane against a single coral curve. Image 2: loose expressive strokes resolving into precise shapes. Image 3: one geometric module repeated with unexpected changes of scale and orientation. Image 4: abstract screen-like planes alongside typographic fragments that form no readable words. Image 5: a sculptural arrangement of translucent and opaque shapes. Image 6: distinct illustrated forms connected through shared lines, suggesting conversation without depicting people. Image 7: an abstract progression from sketch-like marks to a balanced composition. All images are illustrative studies, not evidence of delivered work.
design.brandNotes: Three logo concepts considered: open-frame offers an airy container for changing ideas; interlock connects independent shapes through a shared negative-space seam; ligature gives the long business name a more typographic expression but risks reduced clarity at small sizes. Select interlock: two offset, open geometric forms with a simple silhouette, avoiding literal gears or implied technology credentials. Pair it with the full supplied business name rather than an invented abbreviation. Use a panorama-led introduction, modern typography, generous spacing and an ink-and-paper foundation; reserve plum, teal and coral for artwork and small accents. Alternate expansive images, concise statements and practical inquiry sections instead of repeated cards. Keep synthetic-preview status visible and distinguish inquiry topics from confirmed offerings. All copy, visual directions and privacy wording are drafts for admin review.
